Commentary.Commentary: It was raining for a while but the covers have been removed now as the rain has disappeared. We should be back with chase shortly.
..THE CHASE...

Sri Lanka will be really happy with how things have ended. The start wasn't that good, Dilshan Madushanka in particular had a really bad day at the office but the others made up for him. Dunith Wellalage and Akila Dananjaya bowled in tandem and stopped the run flow at numerous times. Pramod Madushan and Avishka Fernando were brilliant too. This is a chaseable total. The bowlers have done well to restrict Afghanistan to a par total and it is upto the batters to do the job! Can Sri Lanka make it 3-0 or Afghanistan will avoid the whitewash?

Very early to say but Afghanistan have left around 25- 30 runs out in the middle. The way they started, 300 looked very much possible but yet again the lower-order collapsed just like they did in the last game. Rahmanullah Gurbaz scored 17 runs off the first over and gave a blistering start to his team. He played with intent and scored a couple of brilliant shots but fell 2 short of his fifty. The baton though was passed to Rahmat Shah who played a composed innings of 65. Then there was the stand between Azmatullah Omarzai and Ikram Alikhil, both added around 50 runs but fell just when it was time to accelerate. Mohammad Nabi was the last hope but he too didn't make a big difference.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. The players are out in the middle. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran to open for the visitors. Dilshan Madushanka to bowl first.

Kusal Mendis says they don't mind batting first. Informs Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana are rested for this game. Reckons the first two games went according to the plan and are looking forward to bowl first.

Hashmatullah Shahidi says they'll bat as the wicket looks good. Informs about the team changes. Reckons their fielding wasn't upto the mark and also lost wickets in tandems in the last game, so they will look to do better in this game.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Avishka Fernando, Kusal Mendis (C/WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Janith Liyanage, Akila Dananjaya (In for Wanindu Hasaranga), Dunith Wellalage (In for Maheesh Theekshana), Dilshan Madushanka, Asitha Fernando, Pramod Madushan.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Ikram Alikhil (WK), Azmatullah Omarzai, Sharafuddin Ashraf, Mohammad Nabi, Fareed Ahmad, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Qais Ahmad.
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and will BAT.

Two comfortable wins for the hosts has seen them seal the series with a game to go. Despite having a series in the bag, they'll be eager to make it three in three. Afghanistan on the other hand, will look to salvage some pride but avoiding the whitewash. Still a lot to play for, let's hope we get a cracker of a game this time around. Stay tuned for the toss and teams.
... MATCH DAY ...

Afghanistan embarked on their tour to Sri Lanka with high hopes and expectations. However, their journey so far hasn't been fruitful. They suffered a defeat in the one-off Test without much of a challenge. Although they displayed great fighting spirit in the first ODI, they ended up on the losing side. In the second game, they were completely outplayed. With winning the series now out of reach, they can only aim to salvage some pride and avoid a whitewash. Struggling without their formidable spin duo of Rashid Khan and Mujeeb ur Rahman, Afghanistan have conceded 300+ totals in both matches. Noor Ahmad and Qais Ahmad have failed to make a significant impact, while pacers Fazalhaq Farooqi and Fareed Ahmad have also struggled. Their batting has been inconsistent too. In the first game, Mohammad Nabi and Azmatullah Omarzai kept them in contention while chasing a massive target with two huge centuries after the top order failed, but couldn't seal the win. In the previous game, Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmat Shah got half-centuries, but the rest of the batting lineup failed, resulting in a heavy defeat. Omarzai compensated for his batting failure with excellent bowling, emerging as one of the top all-rounders globally. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi's lack of runs is concerning, and they hope to regain it and perform collectively in the upcoming game to challenge the hosts. On the other hand, Sri Lanka can consider themselves somewhat fortunate, with Pathum Nissanka's sensational double hundred in the first game making the difference. Contributions from Avishka Fernando, who narrowly missed a century, were also crucial. In the last ODI, it was more of a collective effort, with Kusal Mendis, Sadeera Samarawickrama, and Janith Liyanage registering fifties, while Asalanka smashed a brilliant 97. The positive for the Lankans is that every batter is in good form, making them a solid unit. Pramod Madushan starred with the ball in the first game, while Wanindu Hasaranga impressed in the second. Although Maheesh Theekshana hasn't taken a wicket in this series, he aims to change that, while Dilshan Madushanka and Asitha Fernando have played vital supporting roles in the bowling department. The hosts are brimming with confidence and aim for a 3-0 series win, while the Afghans seeks a victory to carry momentum into the T20I series. Let's see who emerges victorious.
